full_judgment:
7. The defence case of the present appellants in short is that the alleged confessional statement of convict-Abdul Hasan was not true and voluntary one and same is the outcome of torture of the police, and they have been implicated in the case falsely. 

 10. Ms Sarwat Siraj, the learned Advocate for the appellants, submits that the learned Additional Sessions Judge acted illegally in convicting the appellants inasmuch as the prosecution failed to prove the charge leveled against them beyond reasonable doubt. She further submits that the alleged confessional statement under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure made by convict Abul Hashem is not true and voluntary and same was extracted by threat and putting fear on him though at the time of examination under Section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure convict Abul Hashem stated before the trial Court in what circumstances . he was compelled to make such statement before the Magistrate, but the trial Court in finding the guilty of convict Abul Hashem relying on the said confessional statement did not consider the statement made at the time of examination under Section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, which prejudiced the appellant Abul Hashem and other appellants. She further submits that all the prosecution witnesses are partisan witnesses and save and except PW 5 Ohid Miah, none of the witness saw the occurrence or had identified the assailant. Ms Sarwat seriously argues that PW 5 Ohid Miah cannot be treated as a credible and trustworthy witness as he did not disclose the name of the assailants immediately after the occurrence, rather he disclosed the name of the assailants after a long lapse of time and made a statement under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure before the Magistrate, 1st Class which is an after thought. She also submits that the trial Court did not at all consider the material contradiction of the witnesses, particularly PW 5, who embellished the prosecution story. She referring the case of Abdus Salam Mollah vs State, reported in 13 MLR (AD) 268 and submits that confession of an accused cannot form sole basis of conviction against the Non-confessing accused persons, Jointly tried for the same offence without other corroborative substantive evidence. In this connection she also referees the cases of Ustar Ali vs State, reported in 18 BLD (AD) 42 = 3 BLC (AD) 53 and Babor Ali Molla vs State, reported in 44 DLR (AD) 10. 

 11. On the other hand, Mr Farhad Ahmed, the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing on behalf of the State submits that the trial Court on proper appreciation of the evidence on record rightly found guilty to the accused persons. He further submits that the confessional statement under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure made by convict Abul Hashem is inculpatory in nature and same has been found true and voluntary by the trial Court and, as such, conviction can be based relying on the said confessional statement. He further submits that the prosecution proved the motive of the murder and prays for dismissal of the appeal. 

 14. PW 1, the informant Jharu Miah, is the paternal uncle of deceased-Shahid Miah. He deposed that on the night of occurrence he was sleeping after taking dinner and at about 12-30 O'clock he heard a sound of gunshot and hearing the same he came out from his house and hearing the hue and cry from the western side he rushed to the house of Shahid Miah with Makhan and Dhanu Miah and after reaching there he found that Shahid Miah was lying on a 'Chowki' in his north 'bhiti' teen shed room and sustained bleeding injury under the right hand arm and he succumbed to his injury; Shahid Miah was a teacher of Balighar Hujuri Shah Madrasa, The deceased was gun down from the window of the room. After 10/12 days of the occurrence Ohid Miah the brother of Shahid Master informed him that he could identify the assailants and dis- closed their names as Hashem, Shahjahan, Hossain and others. Before the occurrence a cow of Shahid Master was stolen and the accused persons committed the said theft and a salish was held over the said incident and it was decided in the said salish that the accused persons would be ousted from their village. 

 17. He further deposed that his uncle Ohid Miah came first at the place of occurrence and his grandfather lodged the First Information Report. He is one of the witness of the inquest report 5/6 years back, accused-Shahjahan and Hashem theft two cows from Sham gram and his father after recovering the same returned back to its owner and his father initiated the salish for that. After 10/12 days of the occurrence his Uncle Ohid Mia informed him that Shahjahan and Hossain were arrested and there after he along with Ohid Miah, Farid Miah, Jharu Miah went to the Police Station and at the Police Station they disclosed about the occurrence. 

 18. In cross-examination he stated that at the time of occurrence he was a student of a college and he did not see who shoot on the person of his father, but his uncle Ohid Miah identified the assailants. He denied the suggestion that accused Abul Hashem did not lift any cow, no salish was took place and Abul Hashem did not confess his guilt at the local Police Station. 

 19. PW 3 Rehana Begum, wife of deceased Shahid Miah, deposed that on the night of occurrence, she along with her husband and younger son Sujan were sleeping in western room of Uttar Bhiti house and hearing the sound to the effect ‘মাগো মাগো’ she woke up and put on a light and saw that his husband was felling down on the bed from sitting condition. She found blood, beside the right hand and a cut injury on his waist. She pressed the injured place by her 'sharee' and 'blouse' and thereafter his brother-in-Iaw Ohid Miah came to the room and asked her about the occurrence. In the meantime, so many neighbouring people came to their house. When her brother-in-law Ohid Miah was coming towards their house, he heard a sound of gunshot. At one stage she lost her sense; on the following day her ‘চাচা শশুর’ Jharu Miah, lodged the First Information Report with the Police Station. She further said that after 4/5 days of the occurrence her brother-in-law Ohid Miah informed her that he had indentified accused- Shahjahan and Hossain. But could not identify the other accomplice of them. She indentified accused- Hashem, Shahjahan and Hossain, present in the dock. 

 20. In cross-examination she state that after 4/5 days of the occurrence Ohid Miah disclosed to her the name of Shahjahan and Hossain, as the assailants of her husband. His brother-in-law Ohid Miah was at the house when Jharu Miah went to the police station. She denied the suggestion that Ohid Miah never told her the name of accused-Shahjahan, Hossain and Hashem. 

 22. Hearing the said fact he went to the house of Shahid Master and saw the dead body of Shahid Master. He also stated that accused-Hashem and Shahajahan are full brothers. In the month of May, 1989, accused Hashem disclosed them that they had theft two cows from village Sham gram and thereafter he said cows were returned back to the owner and after 7/8 days of the said incident two cows of Shahid Miah was also stolen by Hashem, Shahjahan and Dhanu and over the same a salish was took place and they were asked to leave the village. But on various plea they did not leave the village. This witness further deposed that he did not see the occurrence. After 5/7 days of the occurrence Ohid Miah informed him that he had identified Shahjahan and Hossain, when they were fleeing away after killing Shahid Miah. 

 26. PW 6 Hamdu Miah, in his deposition stated that after 6/7 months of the occurrence police arrested accused Hashem and hearing the said fact they went to the Police Station and Hashem disclosed to them that Shahjahan, Hossain, Anis and Nuru Miah killed Shahid Master. He also deposed that there was enmity between the deceased and the accused persons over the lifting of cows. 

 27. In cross-examination he failed to say in which date accused Hashem confessed his guilt before them in the police station; on the day of occurrence he was in his house and he failed to recollect when he met with Ohid Miah and Jharu Miah after the occurrence. 

 28. PW 7 Mongal Miah, deposed that after 6/7 months of the occurrence he heard from the villagers that Hashem confessed in the Police Station that he along with Shahjahan, Hossain, Anis and Nuru killed the victim. He also deposed that over the dispute of cow lifting 'Salish' was took place and the accused persons were asked to leave their village. 

 31. PW 10 Abdul Wadud, the Magistrate 1st Class, in his deposition stated that on 11-6-1995 he was serving as Magistrate, Ist Class, Brahmanbaria Sadar; he recorded the statement under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure of accused Abul Hashem. He proved the said statement as Exhibit-2 and his signature on it as Exhibit-2/1; on 29-10-1995 he recorded the statement of witness Ohid Miah and he proved the said statement Exhibit-3 and his signature as Exhibit 3/1. 

 35. PW 13, Shamsul Haque, deposed that accused Hashem disclosed to him that accused- Shahjahan, Anis killed Shahid Master. 

 36. In cross-examination he stated that Hashem did not disclose to him who shot to Shahid Master. He disclosed the said fact to the police after two years of the occurrence. Hashem disclosed the fact of killing in cm office in presence of Jahur Member, Farid Miah and Maju Master; he could not say, when they went to the office of CID. 

 37. PW 14, Santosh Kumar Kundu, in his deposition stated that after completion of the investigation by Mozahar Alam and Rabi Ghosh charge sheet was submitted on 30-1-1995 against accused Shahjahan and Hashem and thereafter upon an application of the informant, the Head Office of CID took up the investigation of the case again; he visited the place of occurrence, made consultation with the previous Investigating Officers and examined the informant and recorded the statement of 3(three) witnesses. He took remand of accused-Hashem and Hashem disclosed the hame of the assailants including his name. The others are Shahjahan, Nuru, Hossain and Anis; he thereafter produced accused- Hashem before the Magistrate, 1st Class, to record his statement under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Before completion his investigation he handed over the 'Case Docate' to Inspector Md Saleh Ahmmed, because of his transfer. 

 38. In cross-examination he stated that after filing of the charge sheet in the Court, the ClD Head Quarter asked him to investigate the case. He had no knowledge whether the informant filed any Naraji against the charge sheet. At the direction of ClD Head Office he took up the investigation. He denied the suggestion that he had compelled accused- Hashem to make confessional statement before the Magistrate. He admitted that before taking Hashem into remand, he was in custody. He denied the suggestion that he did not torture on accused-Hashem, while he was on remand. 

 40. In cross-examination he admitted that in the First Information Report no name of any accused was mentioned. None of the witness stated to him that they saw accused Shahajahan in the place of occurrence. He did not arrest any accused person during his investigation. He did not record any statement of accused-Abul Hashem after examining him. He further deposed that he did not find any evidence against accused-Abul Hashem in Committing the offence. Hashem is a cow lifter no such information was available in the record. He examined accused-Hashem but did not pray for his remand. 

 45. In cross-examination he stated that in the charge sheet it has not been mentioned, whether the informant filed any naraji against the previous charge sheet; as per the direction of Additional Inspector of police CID, he took up the investigation. He could not say the basis to give such order of investigation. He could not record the statement of the witnesses under Section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and he did not take step to record the statement of accused-Shahjahan under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 49. On careful examination and scrutiny of the evidence on record it appears to us that save and except PW-5 Ohid Miah, none of the witness saw the assailants or the occurrence. PW 1 the informant, PW 2 son and PW 3 wife of the deceased and PW- 6, uncle of the deceased and 6 heard the names of the assailants from Ohid Miah. Now let us consider the evidence of Ohid Miah whether his assertion with regard to the identification of the assailants, particularly accused-Shahjahan and Hossain, how far is believable. In the instant case PW 1, Jharu Miah, uncle of the deceased, who was aged about 70 years at the relevant time lodged the First Information Report with the police station without mentioning any name of any accused or even did not suspect or disclose any name out of suspicion. Though, from the evidence of PW 1 Jharu Miah, it is evident that before going to the police station he had consulted with PW 5 Ohid Miah. PW 1 in his deposition stated that after 10/12 days of the occurrence Ohid Miah disclosed that he identified the assailants namely, Hashem, Shahjahan and Hossain. But PW 3 Rehana Begum in her deposition stated that around 4/5 days after the occurrence Ohid Miah informed her that he could recognize the assailants namely, Shahajahan and Hossain PW 5 Ohid Miah himself in his deposition stated that he disclosed the name of Hossain dacoit only before the police PW 1 mentioned 3 (three) names that is Shahjahan, Hashem and Hossain, PW 3 mentioned the name of accused Shahajahan and Hossain, but PW 5 Ohid Miah mentioned the name of Hossain only. This material contradiction as to the manner and number of disclosing the name of the assailants creates a reason able doubt dbout veracity of the statement of PW 5 Ohid Miah.Further belated discloser of the names of the assailants by PW 5, possibility of embellishment and concoction of the prosecution case by the said witness cannot be ruled out. It is by now settled principle of law that delay in disclosing the names, of assailants cast a serious doubt as to the truthfulness of the testimony of a witness and the chance of concoction and false implicatioh cannot be ruled out and, as such, the evidence should be left out of consideration. In instant case, the PW 5 Ohid Miah a statement under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure before the Magistrate, 1st class on 29-10-1995 long after 1 year and 4 months of the alleged occurrence, Further in his cross examination he admitted that "দারোগার কাছে আমি শুধু হোসেন ডাকাত বলেছি।” In view of the above facts and circumstances and proposition of law, it is very difficult for us to rely the evidence of PW 5 Ohid Miah as a credible and trustworthy witness and testimony should be left out of consideration. 

 50. In the instant case the trial Court found the confessional statement under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure of accused-Abul Hashem is true and voluntary and relying on the same awarded the conviction to its maker Abul Hashem and the other co-accused. The statement under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure made by convict-Abul Hashem is as follows: 

 51. If we consider these features of the confessional statements we have no hesitation to hold that the alleged confessional statements is almost exculpatory in nature, save and except 'আমাদের ৪ জনের হাতে লাঠি ছিল; But convict Abdul Hashem neither took part in making the decision of killing, nor took active in committing the murder, rather he was sitting in a ‘পাট ক্ষেত' (Jute field). 

 52. It appears from record that convict Abul Hashem wa,s arrested on 23-1-1995 and on that day he Was taken remand for 4(four) days and after ending of the said period of remand he was produced before the Court on 30-1-1995 and he was sent to the jail hajat. 

 53. Police submitted charge sheet on 11-2- 1995 and when the said charge sheet was awaiting for acceptance at that time the Criminal Investigating Department filed an application before the Court of the learned Magistrate on 27-3-1995 for Case Docate and PW 14 Santosh Kumar Kundu, the new investigating officer of CID took convict-AbuI Hashem on remand for 3(three) days and after said remand convict-AbuI Hashem had made the alleged confessional statement before Magistrate. 

 54. PW 10 Abdul Wadud, the Magistrate who recorded the statement of accused-AbuI Hashem in his cross-examination admitted to the effect: 

 55. These assertions of PW 10 prove that he recorded the confessional statement of convict Abul Hashem In a very mechanical and casual manner violating the provision of section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The recording Magistrate did not make any genuine effort to find out the real character of the confession. In the case of Alauddin Khan Pathan vs State, reported in 19 BLD 74 refers by the learned Advocate for the Appellants, it has been held that; 

 "The recording Magistrate is bound to make a real and substantial inquiry as to voluntariness of the confession, in doing so, the Magistrate must put questions to the confessing accused to find out if the confession is made out of repentance or for any other good reason or whether it is the result of torturing or tutoring by somebody or whether it has been caused by any inducement, threat or promise". 

 56. In the case of State vs Babul Miah, reported in 63 DLR (AD) 10, it has been held: 

 57. If we consider the evidence of PW 10, the Magistrate, who recorded the alleged confessional statement of convict Abul Hashem, with the above proposition of law and the facts that convict-Abul Hashem made the statement before the Magistrate after his second time remand and before that he was in Jail hajat quite a long time after his first remand, it is very difficult for us to hold that the alleged confessional statement of Abul Hashem is true and voluntary one and he made the said statement voluntarily without fear. Consequently, these are of no legal consequence and this confessional statement must be kept out of consideration. 

 62. We are of the view that the motive which has put forwarded by the prosecution does not inspire any confidence that after along lapse of time of the alleged Salish, the accused persons in order to take revenge had killed Shahid Master. More so, the prosecution witnesses contradicts each other on this fact also. 

 63. Since we have already held that the confessional statement of convict-AbuI Hashem is not true and voluntary and there is no other direct or circumstantial evidence to substantiate the same, rather the prosecution particularly PW 5 Ohid Miah the alleged eye witness embellished the prosecution story, we are of the view that the conviction of accused Abul Hashem cannot be sustained. The conviction of appellants, Nuru Miah and Shahjahan, who have convicted relying on the confessional statement of co-accused-Abul Hashem is not legal and unwarranted in Iaw. It is by now settled principle of law that confession of a co. accused cannot be the sole basis to convict the other of the co-accused, in absence of other corroborative evidence. In the instant case there is no other substantial evidence against convict-Nuru Miah and Shahjahan, to corroborate the confessional statement of accused-AbuI Hashem. 

 65. In the result, the appeal is allowed. The judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 21-6-2001 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, 2nd Court, Brahmanbaria in Sessions Case No. 121 of 1996 convicting the appellants under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code and sentencing them to suffer imprisonment for life with a fine of Taka 10,000 each, in default, to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 6(six) months is hereby set aside. The appellants are acquitted from the charges leveled against them. The appellants Nos. 1 and 2, who are on bail be discharged from their respective bail bonds. The appellant No.3 Abul Hashem alias Hashem who has been languishing in Jail more than 16(sixteen) years released from the Jail immediately, if not wanted in any other case.
